evals.prompt: Write the core of a Go worker that uses cirello.io/dynamolock/v5 to process one campaign at a time with DynamoDB. It should use AWS SDK v2, a 30-second lease, a 5-second heartbeat, bounded acquisition, and safe release.
evals.expected_output: The example uses the v5 module and AWS SDK v2 imports, configures a compatible lease/heartbeat pair, acquires with a context, and releases the owned lock while handling errors.
assertions: The example uses github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2 configuration and DynamoDB client packages
Acquisition uses a bounded context or an explicit cancellation path
The acquired lock is released and release errors are not silently treated as success

evals.prompt: Design leader election with dynamolock. Explain how to configure heartbeats, detect a degraded lease, and what the service must do when the session monitor fires.
evals.expected_output: The design uses automatic heartbeats with a safe lease margin, registers a session monitor, and stops leadership/protected work when the callback fires or heartbeat ownership becomes uncertain.
assertions: The design keeps heartbeat period at no more than half the lease
The design uses WithSessionMonitor with a safe time before expiration
The callback stops leadership or protected work rather than continuing
The design treats heartbeat failure as possible loss of ownership

evals.prompt: A service should immediately report that a lock is busy and separately inspect who owns a lock. Show the dynamolock calls and error checks, including the important limitation of Get.
evals.expected_output: The answer uses FailIfLocked and errors.As for LockNotGrantedError, uses Get for observation, and explains that a lock returned by Get is read-only for heartbeat/release purposes.
assertions: The busy result is checked with errors.As and LockNotGrantedError
The observation path uses Get without treating it as acquisition
The answer warns that a Get result cannot be used for heartbeat ownership
